facts.value: no later than the next regular payday for that pay
facts.summary: New York: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due no later than the next regular payday for that pay.
facts.evidence_quote: Employees whose employment has ended are entitled to be paid no later than the pay day on which their next pay would have been due had they still been employed. Upon request of the employee, employers are required to mail the employee his or her wages.
facts.source_title: Frequency of Pay Frequently Asked Questions (NYS DOL)
facts.source_publisher: New York State Department of Labor
facts.notes: NY Labor Law Section 191. FAQ covers termination, retirement, or resignation.

facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $17.00 (New York City, Nassau County, Suffolk County, & Westchester County); $16.00 (remainder of the state) Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 The New York minimum wage equals the federal minimum wage when set below the federal rate. Residential workers ("live-in workers") receive premium pay for hours worked over 44 in a payroll week. Employers operating a factory, mercantile establishment, hotel, restaurant, freight/passenger elevator, or theater; or a building employing security guards, janitors, superintendents, managers, engineers, or fireme

facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page. Regional rates: value_numeric left empty so no single figure acts as a statewide default.

facts.value: Manual workers weekly (within 7 days of week end); clerical and other workers at least semi-monthly
facts.summary: New York pay frequency rule: Manual workers weekly (within 7 days of week end); clerical and other workers at least semi-monthly.
facts.evidence_quote: Manual Workers: Wages must be paid weekly and not later than seven calendar days after the end of the week in which the wages are earned. ... Clerical or Other Workers: Wages must be paid in accordance with the agreed terms of employment and not less frequently than semi-monthly.
facts.source_title: Frequency of Pay Frequently Asked Questions (NYS DOL)
facts.source_publisher: New York State Department of Labor

facts.summary: New York is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)

facts.summary: New York 2026 new employer UI rate: 4.025% (3.4% normal + 0.625% subsidiary); 4.1% total with the 0.075% Re-employment Service Fund.
facts.evidence_quote: For liability beginning in 2025 or 2026, use the following rates to calculate your UI Contributions due. ... For wages paid during: 2025 ... 4.025% 2026 ... 4.025% UI Rates include: Normal Rate 3.4% Subsidiary Rate 0.625% UI Rate 4.025%
facts.source_title: IA 98: Notice of Unemployment Insurance Contribution Rates (NYS DOL)
facts.source_publisher: New York State Department of Labor
facts.notes: Rate basis: base UI rate (3.4% normal + 0.625% subsidiary) for employers whose liability began in 2025 or 2026. The 0.075% Re-employment Service Fund is added on top for a 4.1% total (see NY.ui.total_new_employer_rate). IA 98 shows 4.325% for 2026 for employers whose liability began in 2023 or 2024.

facts.summary: New York 2026 UI contribution rate range: 1.7% to 9.5% total.
facts.evidence_quote: For 2026, the range of New York State unemployment insurance contribution rates is as follows: Rate Information Total Lowest rate: 1.7% New Employer rate: 4.1% Highest rate: 9.5%
facts.source_title: General Rate Information (New York State Department of Labor)
facts.source_publisher: New York State Department of Labor
facts.notes: Rate basis: total (normal + subsidiary + 0.075% Re-employment Services Fund).

facts.summary: New York state unemployment taxable wage base: $17,600 per employee.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026

facts.summary: New York 2026 total new employer rate: 4.1% (4.025% UI + 0.075% Re-employment Service Fund).
facts.evidence_quote: For 2026, the range of New York State unemployment insurance contribution rates is as follows: Rate Information Total Lowest rate: 1.7% New Employer rate: 4.1% Highest rate: 9.5%
facts.source_title: General Rate Information (New York State Department of Labor)
facts.source_publisher: New York State Department of Labor
facts.notes: Includes the 0.075% Re-employment Service Fund contribution. 4.1% applies to employers whose liability began in 2025 or 2026; employers whose liability began in 2023 or 2024 pay a 4.325% UI rate in 2026 (plus the 0.075% RSF) (https://forms.labor.ny.gov/UI/IA98.pdf).
